# Acceptance matrix

This file is the normative oracle for the acceptance corpus. Each row names a
fixture construct and its expected behavior at the boundaries exercised by the
MVP. A dash means that the construct must have no independently observable
behavior in that column; it does not mean that the behavior is unspecified.

The tables use canonical, directory-style URLs. A route ending in `/` is written
as an `index.html` file beneath that directory. API routes use the extracted
qualified name beneath `/packages/<slug>/api/`; authored routes retain the path
beneath the collection mount; and concept routes use `/concepts/<id>/`. These
routes are independent of semantic IDs. Only an `index` source occupies its
collection root; `python/docs/guide.qmd` therefore maps to
`/packages/python/guide/guide/`.

The checked-in default workspace is the diagnostic-free baseline. Its sibling
[case overlays](../acceptance-cases) are outside declared input roots. The
[case registry](CASES.json) selects the configuration and at most one overlay,
and records the complete expected diagnostic list separately for `check` and
`build`. Paths in diagnostic records are relative to the materialized workspace;
portable product locations additionally carry the corresponding repository ID.

The tests copy the baseline into a temporary directory, then apply only the
selected case's declared files. Positive visibility and relationship cases
select their existing configurations without overlays. The incompatible
relationship case selects its own configuration against the clean API sources.

The following invariants apply to every row:

- `diplodocus check` parses, extracts, and validates the construct but never starts
  a language runtime or kernel, reads or writes the execution cache, writes
  execution assets, or creates the output directory.
- `None` in the Diagnostic column means that the construct itself produces no
  diagnostic. A row naming a diagnostic gives the sole intentional diagnostic
  for that focused invalid construct; unrelated diagnostics fail its test.
- Every source location contains a repository ID and normalized,
  forward-slash-separated repository-relative path, plus a span where the
  selected parser supplies one; successful Rd nodes currently retain file-level
  provenance rather than fabricated ranges. Portable IR, diagnostics, provenance, rendered
  output, and search data contain no absolute checkout or temporary paths.
- Repository provenance contains the configured canonical URL, revision, dirty
  state when available, and a fingerprint of declared inputs. Extracted API
  provenance also contains extractor identity, version, capabilities, static
  mode, and relevant parser versions. Authored provenance contains the content
  format and Panache version. Executed output provenance additionally contains
  engine and kernel identities and versions, normalized options, declared
  environment fingerprints, the producing cell, and fresh-or-cache status.
- A public item is linkable, appears in its ecosystem-aware package navigation,
  and contributes a search entry containing its package and ecosystem. An
  internal item is linkable and searchable but its unit is absent from the
  project package switcher. A hidden item is linkable by semantic ID but absent
  from navigation and search.
- Authored source links, ordinary relative links, and semantic references are
  validated. Search indexes authored titles and prose, API qualified names,
  signatures, and documentation—not code-cell output or unsupported raw
  syntax.

## MVP completion coverage

Every criterion in `TODO.md` has a stable ID and maps to concrete scenarios.
Registry entries are specifications, not evidence that a future command already
works. Milestone 1 verifies corpus completeness, configuration/input integrity,
case isolation, and the available parser and kernel probes. Later milestones
must execute their scenario actions and compare the specified results before
claiming those product behaviors.

| MVP criterion | Required scenarios |
| --- | --- |
| `MVP-01`: Explicit workspace configuration | `workspace-model` |
| `MVP-02`: Static Python and R APIs | `static-apis`, `offline-static-boundary` |
| `MVP-03`: In-process authored parsing | `authored-profiles`, `own-docs-parse` |
| `MVP-04`: Structured Python and R execution | `structured-execution` |
| `MVP-05`: Shared safe renderer and site model | `site-navigation-search`, `authority-and-output` |
| `MVP-06`: Command contract | `command-options`, `check-without-effects`, `build-outcomes`, `serve-http`, `serve-source-edit`, `serve-environment-edit`, `serve-ignored-edits`, `serve-failure-recovery` |
| `MVP-07`: Deterministic portable builds | `portable-repeat-builds`, `own-docs-portability` |
| `MVP-08`: No implicit installation, network, or execution | `offline-static-boundary`, `authority-and-output`, `new-user-quick-start` |
| `MVP-09`: Full acceptance test stack | `acceptance-test-stack` |
| `MVP-10`: Self-documentation | `own-docs-parse`, `own-docs-build-preview`, `own-docs-portability`, `own-docs-publication` |
| `MVP-11`: New-user workflow | `new-user-quick-start` |

watched or repeated operation. Edits mentioned here affect only that copy.

fixture, and protocol tests may establish part of that evidence earlier.

## Real project documentation behavior

The root `diplodocus.toml` is the real project configuration. The temporary-copy
helper includes its declared pages, assets, and environment input, without
copying output, caches, or unrelated contributor documents. The default `site/`
output is ignored and lies outside both declared content roots. The generated
project landing route is `/`; the guide and examples mount at `/guide/` and
`/examples/`.

| Fixture construct | Expected IR | Diagnostic | Execution | Provenance | URL | Navigation | Link | Concept | Search |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Root `diplodocus.toml` | Content-only workspace with one repository and two project-owned collections, no packages or API targets | None | Only the examples collection authorizes Python | Repository URL and declared `devenv.lock` fingerprint | `/` | Project Guide and Examples sections | No invented package targets | None | Project and authored content |
| `docs/guide/index.md` | Heading, prose, ordinary links, and checked-in image | None | Never | Repository-relative authored source and Panache version | `/guide/` | Guide landing | All four source links and image resolve | None | Title and prose |
| `docs/guide/quick-start.md` | Authored workflow instructions with display-only console fences | None | Never | Repository-relative source | `/guide/quick-start/` | Guide child | Configuration and CLI links resolve | None | Title and explanatory prose |
| `docs/guide/configuration.md` | Prose, table, and display-only TOML | None | Never | Repository-relative source | `/guide/configuration/` | Guide child | Overview and quick-start links resolve | None | Title, table, and prose |
| `docs/guide/cli.md` | Command table and authored contract | None | Never | Repository-relative source | `/guide/cli/` | Guide child | Quick-start link resolves | None | Command names and prose |
| `docs/guide/assets/workspace.svg` | Checked-in local asset | None | Never | Repository-relative asset and fingerprint | `/guide/assets/workspace.svg` | None | Overview image resolves within guide boundary | None | Owning image alt text only |
| `docs/examples/stateful.qmd` | Four ordered Python cells, callout, streams, Markdown, and SVG output | None | One explicitly authorized `python3` session, retaining `total = 12`; check runs no cells | Source, producing cells, kernel identity, and environment fingerprint | `/examples/stateful/` plus local hashed SVG | Examples child | Cross-collection overview and quick-start links resolve | None | Authored title/prose; outputs are excluded |
